Part A: Software Requirements Specification (SRS)

Suggested Artifact: docs/srs.md | Weight: 10 Points | Demonstrates: Stakeholders, Context, Actors, Product Scope, Numbered FR/BR/NFR, Assumptions & Decisions.

1. Stakeholder Problem & System Context

1.1 Stakeholder Problem Statement

Higher education institutions, academic faculties, student affair departments, course lecturers, and student clubs (Survey Owners) routinely conduct evaluations regarding course instruction, library learning environments, dining services, campus Wi-Fi infrastructure, and student activities. However, relying on generic paper forms or consumer-grade online survey tools introduces significant software engineering and data integrity failures:

  • Uncontrolled Duplicate Submissions & Identity Leakage: Standard forms either allow unrestricted, untraceable repeat submissions or tightly bind student accounts to their answers, eliminating genuine anonymity and causing social desirability bias in sensitive campus feedback.
  • Absence of Role-Based & Institutional Access Boundaries: Generic tools lack fine-grained role segregation. An instructor can inadvertently view, modify, or delete another instructor's course evaluations, violating privacy and departmental isolation.
  • Data Corruption Caused by Post-Publish Mutations: Allowing question options or ratings to be modified while responses are being actively submitted breaks historical validity and produces corrupted aggregate summaries.

1.2 Chosen Domain Context: Pollipop

Pollipop is a modern, cloud-ready three-tier web application specifically engineered for university course reviews and campus evaluations. The system manages the full survey lifecycle: structured survey creation (Single Choice and Rating Scale), lifecycle state transitions (DRAFT → PUBLISHED → CLOSED), authenticated response submission within atomic database transactions, strict duplicate prevention, and real-time server-side aggregate calculation.

The system is packaged with multi-stage Docker containers, making it ready for horizontal autoscaling on Google Cloud Platform (Cloud Run and Cloud SQL) per CPE 334 Lab 5 requirements.

2. Actors and Role-Based Responsibilities

Actor / Role Role Code Allowed Operations Explicitly Forbidden Operations
Survey Owner
(Instructor / Staff)		 OWNER - Create new surveys in DRAFT status with Single Choice (2–10 options) and Rating (1–5) questions.
- Inspect, update (while in DRAFT status only), and transition survey state to PUBLISHED or CLOSED.
- Inspect real-time server-calculated aggregate analytics of surveys they own. 		- Forbidden: Accessing, modifying, publishing, or inspecting summaries of surveys owned by other owners (403 Forbidden).
- Forbidden: Submitting responses to any survey as a respondent (403 Forbidden).
Survey Respondent
(Student / University Member)		 RESPONDENT - View open (PUBLISHED) surveys with personal completion status (answered: true / false).
- Submit a validated response exactly once per survey.
- Review own submitted answers in IDENTIFIED mode via GET /api/responses/:id. 		- Forbidden: Creating, modifying, publishing, or closing surveys (403 Forbidden).
- Forbidden: Viewing DRAFT surveys in listing or detail queries (404 Not Found).
- Forbidden: Viewing aggregate summary analytics (403 Forbidden).
- Forbidden: Viewing other respondents' submissions (403 Forbidden).

3. Numbered Functional Requirements (FR)

FR ID Observable Requirement Behavior Sprint
FR-01User Login & Session Creation: Authenticate via email/password, verify bcrypt hash, set HTTP-only pollipop_sid cookie.Sprint 1
FR-02Current User Profile & Logout: Retrieve profile (GET /api/auth/me) and destroy session (POST /api/auth/logout) with cache invalidation.Sprint 1
FR-03Health & Readiness Probes: GET /api/health (liveness) and GET /api/ready (readiness with database SELECT 1).Sprint 1
FR-04Create Draft Survey: OWNER creates survey with title, description, mode (IDENTIFIED), and questions in DRAFT status.Sprint 1
FR-05Sprint 1 Question Types: Accept SINGLE_CHOICE (2–10 options) and RATING (1–5) questions with required flag.Sprint 1
FR-06Publish Survey: OWNER transitions survey from DRAFT to PUBLISHED (making it active for respondents).Sprint 1
FR-07List Surveys by Role: OWNER sees own surveys; RESPONDENT sees PUBLISHED surveys with answered and responseId.Sprint 1
FR-08Submit Validated Response: RESPONDENT submits answers inside an atomic database transaction.Sprint 1
FR-09View Own Submitted Response: In IDENTIFIED mode, RESPONDENT inspects submitted answers via GET /api/responses/:id.Sprint 1
FR-10View Survey Aggregate Summary: OWNER retrieves server-calculated statistics (counts, percentages, mean rating).Sprint 1
FR-11Edit Draft Survey: OWNER updates title, description, or questions while in DRAFT status.Sprint 2
FR-12Close Survey & Expiration: Manual close (POST /api/surveys/:id/close) or scheduled closing (closesAt).Sprint 1 / 2
FR-13Anonymous Survey Mode: Decouple participation tracking from answer storage (respondentId = null).Sprint 2
FR-14Department Eligibility: Restrict survey answering to students matching targetDepartment.Sprint 2
FR-15Extended Question Types: Multi-select (MULTIPLE_CHOICE) and open feedback (SHORT_TEXT).Sprint 2
FR-16Export Survey Results: Download summary analytics and anonymized responses as CSV files.Sprint 3

4. Numbered Business Rules (BR)

BR ID Domain Rule Description Enforced Layer
BR-01Single Submission per Respondent: Duplicate attempts return 409 Conflict (ALREADY_SUBMITTED) backed by DB unique constraint (surveyId, userId) on SurveyParticipation.Application & DB
BR-02Responses Allowed Only on Published Surveys: Answering DRAFT returns 404 Not Found; answering CLOSED returns 409 Conflict (SURVEY_NOT_OPEN).Application
BR-03One-Way Survey Lifecycle State Machine: States progress DRAFT → PUBLISHED → CLOSED. Reversing state returns 409 Conflict (INVALID_STATE_TRANSITION).Application
BR-04Survey Ownership Isolation: OWNER cannot access, edit, publish, close, or inspect summaries of surveys owned by others (403 Forbidden).Application
BR-05Role Segregation: RESPONDENT cannot author/publish surveys or view summaries; OWNER cannot submit responses (403 Forbidden).Application
BR-06Cross-Response Privacy: RESPONDENT can only view own submitted answers; inspecting another user's answers returns 403 Forbidden.Application
BR-07Draft Survey Visibility Restriction: RESPONDENT cannot view or retrieve DRAFT surveys (404 Not Found).Application
BR-08Question & Option Structural Constraints: Survey must have 1–50 questions. SINGLE_CHOICE must have 2–10 non-empty options.Application
BR-09Answer Completeness & Validity: Required questions must be answered. Options must belong to the question. Rating must be 1–5. Optional questions may be omitted.Application & DB
BR-10Server-Side Aggregate Accuracy: Statistics computed server-side to 2 decimal places. Handles zero responses without division by zero.Application
BR-11Immutability After Publication: Modifying questions/options after publication is forbidden (409 Conflict).Application
BR-12Sprint 1 Baseline Eligibility: All authenticated students can answer any published survey.Application
BR-13True Anonymity Separation: In ANONYMOUS mode, Response.respondentId is strictly null.Application & DB

5. Numbered Non-Functional Requirements (NFR)

NFR ID Category Measurable Target Practical Verification Method
NFR-01Security & Cache GuardUnauthenticated requests rejected with 401 100% of the time. Cache-Control: no-store on protected endpoints. Browser back redirect to /login on revoked sessions.Supertest API integration + Playwright E2E browser history test (TEST-39, TEST-40).
NFR-02Password & Secret HygienePasswords hashed with bcrypt (salt rounds ≥ 10). Zero plaintext secrets in Git, logs, or client bundle.Database seed inspection (TEST-38) + git index audit against .env.example.
NFR-03Data Integrity & ConcurrencyConcurrent duplicate submissions result in exactly one 201 Created and one 409 Conflict with atomic rollback.Database unique constraint + Promise.all concurrent test (TEST-37).
NFR-04Validation & Error StandardZod schema validation returning structured 400 Bad Request with dot-path notation and sanitized messages.Zod unit tests & Supertest invalid payload tests (TEST-03, TEST-11, TEST-24).
NFR-05Cloud-ReadinessAll configurations read from environment. Probes /api/health & /api/ready respond in < 500 ms. Sessions survive restarts.Supertest health probe tests (TEST-07, TEST-08) + Docker packaging.

Part C: System-Level Software Design Specification (SDS)

Suggested Artifact: docs/system-sds.md | Weight: 15 Points | Demonstrates: Architecture, ERD, Security, Role Matrix, and GCP Cloud Run Deployment Plan.

1. Three-Tier Architectural Design

Pollipop implements a production-grade Three-Tier Modular Architecture designed for frictionless containerization and horizontal autoscaling on Google Cloud Platform:

Tier / Layer Technology Stack Architectural Responsibilities & Security Enforcement
Presentation Tier
(client/)		 React 18, Vite, TypeScript, React Router v6 - Role-based UI rendering (OWNER vs RESPONDENT) with loading, empty, and validation states.
- Automatic credential propagation (credentials: 'include').
- Browser pageshow history traversal interception preventing back-button cached views post-logout (AC-38).
Application / API Tier
(server/)		 Node.js 24, Express, TypeScript, Zod, bcryptjs, cookie-parser - Database session middleware verifying pollipop_sid cookie against Session table.
- Cache-Control: no-store injection on all protected routes.
- Role & ownership verification enforcing BR-04, BR-05, and BR-06.
- Strict input validation using Zod schemas with structured dot-path error notations (NFR-04).
Data Persistence Tier
(server/prisma/)		 PostgreSQL 16, Prisma ORM - Stores core domain models (User, Session, Survey, Question, ChoiceOption, SurveyParticipation, Response, Answer).
- Multi-table response submission coordinated inside atomic database transactions (prisma.$transaction).
- Unique constraint @@unique([surveyId, userId]) on SurveyParticipation for race-condition prevention (BR-01, NFR-03).

2. Data Model & Entity-Relationship Design (ERD)

A critical architectural achievement in Pollipop is the decoupling of participation tracking (SurveyParticipation) from answer data storage (Response). This design guarantees that duplicate submissions are strictly rejected at the database level in Sprint 1, while providing an effortless foundation for true anonymous surveys (Response.respondentId = null) in Sprint 2 without modifying constraints.

Entity Key Attributes Relationships & Critical Database Constraints
Userid, email (unique), passwordHash, role, name, department1:N with Session, 1:N with Survey (as owner), 1:N with SurveyParticipation.
Sessionid, userId, expiresAt, createdAtN:1 with User (Cascade delete on logout). Stores HTTP-only session tokens.
Surveyid, title, description, status (DRAFT/PUBLISHED/CLOSED), mode, ownerIdN:1 with User (owner). 1:N with Question, 1:N with SurveyParticipation, 1:N with Response.
Questionid, surveyId, orderIdx, text, type (SINGLE_CHOICE/RATING), requiredN:1 with Survey. 1:N with ChoiceOption. 1:N with Answer.
ChoiceOptionid, questionId, orderIdx, textN:1 with Question. 1:N with Answer. (2–10 choices for single-choice questions).
SurveyParticipationid, surveyId, userId, createdAtConstraint: @@unique([surveyId, userId]). Enforces single submission at DB level.
Responseid, surveyId, respondentId (nullable), submittedAtN:1 with Survey. In IDENTIFIED mode, respondentId links to User; in ANONYMOUS, it is null.
Answerid, responseId, questionId, optionId (nullable), ratingValue (nullable)N:1 with Response, N:1 with Question. Nullable fields support optional questions cleanly.

4. Cloud Readiness & Deployment Architecture (Lab 5 GCP Plan)

Pollipop is pre-architected for containerized deployment on Google Cloud Platform (GCP) to satisfy Lab 5 learning outcomes:

  • Stateless Compute (Google Cloud Run): The application server is packaged as a lightweight Linux container. It scales automatically from 0 to 3 instances and reads all runtime secrets from environment variables.
  • Managed Persistence (Google Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL 16): User sessions and survey datasets are persisted externally. Cloud SQL survives container redeployments and restarts (R-04).
  • Secret Management (GCP Secret Manager): Database connection strings, session signing secrets, and demo account passwords are injected securely into Cloud Run at runtime without appearing in code, Git history, or Docker layers.
  • Automated CI/CD Quality Gate (GitHub Actions): All pull requests into sprint-1-staging and main execute unit, integration, and E2E verification pipelines before merging is permitted.

3. Test Excerpts of Domain Rule & Role Ownership (Protocol Section 4.2)

3.1 Important Domain Rule: Atomic Duplicate Response Prevention (BR-01 / AC-21 / TEST-21)

// Location: server/tests/responses.test.ts
it('TEST-21 / AC-21: Duplicate response submission returns 409 Conflict (ALREADY_SUBMITTED)', async () => {
  const payload = {
    answers: [
      { questionId: singleChoiceQ.id, optionId: singleChoiceQ.options[0].id },
      { questionId: ratingQ.id, ratingValue: 5 }
    ]
  };

  // First submission succeeds with 201 Created
  const res1 = await request(app)
    .post(`/api/surveys/${publishedSurvey.id}/responses`)
    .set('Cookie', studentCookie)
    .send(payload);
  expect(res1.status).toBe(201);

  // Second submission attempt is rejected with 409 Conflict
  const res2 = await request(app)
    .post(`/api/surveys/${publishedSurvey.id}/responses`)
    .set('Cookie', studentCookie)
    .send(payload);
  expect(res2.status).toBe(409);
  expect(res2.body.error.code).toBe('ALREADY_SUBMITTED');
});

3.2 Role & Ownership Restriction: Ownership Isolation (BR-04 / AC-32 / TEST-32)

// Location: server/tests/summary.test.ts
it('TEST-32 / AC-32: Non-owning OWNER (owner2) querying summary receives 403 Forbidden', async () => {
  const survey = await createPublishedSurvey(owner1Cookie);

  // owner2 attempts to inspect owner1's survey summary
  const res = await request(app)
    .get(`/api/surveys/${survey.id}/summary`)
    .set('Cookie', owner2Cookie);

  expect(res.status).toBe(403);
  expect(res.body.error.code).toBe('FORBIDDEN');
  expect(res.body.error.message).toContain('You do not own this survey');
});

6. AI-Use Declaration & Supervised Engineering

In accordance with CPE 334 course guidelines, generative AI agents were utilized as pair-programming assistants under active human engineering supervision. The division of responsibility was maintained as follows:

  • AI Assistance: Generating initial boilerplate scaffolding, TypeScript interfaces, and CSS pastel color variable candidates.
  • Human Engineering Supervision: Formulating domain business rules, architecting the decoupled SurveyParticipation schema, auditing session security and cache headers, reviewing PR diffs, and executing automated test suites. Zero unverified code was merged into the repository.

7. Known Limitations & Disclosures (Sprint 1 Scope)

  • Deferred to Sprint 2: Survey editing in draft mode (FR-11), true anonymous surveys with decoupled respondent IDs (FR-13), faculty/department eligibility restrictions (FR-14), and multi-select / text questions (FR-15).
  • Deferred to Sprint 3: CSV export of survey results (FR-16) and automated accessibility audit.
  • Automated Test Status: 46 total automated tests executed; 46 passed (100% pass rate, 0 failures, 0 skips).

8. Local Reproduction & Safe Test Access Guide

# 1. Clone repository and install dependencies
git clone https://github.com/phatthidawadi/pollipop.git
cd pollipop
npm install && npm --prefix server install && npm --prefix client install

# 2. Setup environment variables and database seed
cp server/.env.example server/.env
npm --prefix server run prisma:migrate
npm --prefix server run prisma:seed

# 3. Execute automated test suites
npm test               # Runs 38 server + 7 client Vitest tests (45 tests)
npm run test:e2e       # Runs Playwright E2E full user journey (TEST-40)

# 4. Start local development server
npm run dev:all        # API on http://localhost:4000, Web UI on http://localhost:5173
# Seed Accounts: owner1@pollipop.local (OWNER) | student1@pollipop.local (RESPONDENT)
# Password: read from DEMO_USER_PASSWORD in server/.env (default: ChangeMeInDev123!)
